summary.intent: Get the pending changesets rewritten to a user-focused convention and published as a PR, then move on to alpha-release readiness: the failing release pipeline, alpha docs, and the oracle benchmark run against real corpora.
summary.outcome: Opened PR #488 (trail 405) with all ten changesets rewritten plus a new one for #485 and a fixed storybook-parity.md row. Gathered preliminary oracle numbers for four corpora, diagnosed the release failure as E167 from the unfinished 0.11.0 release, and paused for the user's choice on recovery. Only packages/storybook/README.md was modified in this stretch.

repo: AGENTS.md defines the changeset convention: a bold lead-in naming the change as users see it, bullets for why/how to adopt/limits, a separate **Breaking:** paragraph with an **Action:** line for breaking changes, and no internals such as struct fields, cache schema numbers or ADR numbers.
Verification commands are `just lint`, `just doc-check machete typos` and `just semver`.

The 'Execute approved release' CI failure is the unfinished 0.11.0 release hitting E167 on every main push. docs/releasing.md gives two recoveries: delete the mismatched asset and re-dispatch, or move RELEASE_PENDING_FROM past it.

The oracle run lives in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/. weekly.json holds per-corpus caliper/rdt/headline/recall data, logs/loads.txt records machine load, and the final report goes to REPORT.md.
The addon's new collapseInheritedProps default is 'dependencies'; setting it to 'none' keeps every inherited prop. This is a breaking change that needs a user-facing note.
workflow: Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user approval. The assistant checked the pushed branch itself (read one changeset in full) before opening the PR.
Release-affecting actions (deleting assets, re-dispatching, moving RELEASE_PENDING_FROM) were held for explicit user approval.

Benchmark wall times are unreliable when machine load is high. The harness waited 900 s for quiet and then ran anyway, so timings should be re-run on an idle machine while memory and output size stay valid.
Use `python3 -I` when reading JSON from fixture directories, as the environment guidance recommends.

friction: `git fetch` was blocked for the subagent, so it branched from an existing origin/main ref rather than a fresh one.
The oracle weekly ran under heavy load (averages 6.7–8.6, 12.7 over 15 minutes at the start), inflating all wall times, partly due to another agent's build.
Chakra has no headline row in the oracle output, possibly a failed oracle step.
Mantine has 12,681 of 20,148 props 'not judged', which makes its correctness rate hard to interpret.
open_items: User decision needed on the E167 release failure: delete the mismatched asset and re-dispatch, or move RELEASE_PENDING_FROM.
Read the nine other rewritten changesets before the release PR; only the collapse one was read in full.

Wait for the oracle worker to finish: Spectrum numbers, Chakra headline, first-vs-second-run script, Storybook dev mode measurements and the 0.11.0 comparison. Then re-time first and second runs on an idle machine for the official numbers.
Investigate why Mantine has so many 'not judged' props and why Chakra has no headline row.
Docs still to do: STATUS.md numbers, MIGRATING.md and README limits. An alpha docs subagent was dispatched for the addon upgrade note and known limits.
Open decisions: audience for the alpha, and whether the addon default flip ships in the first alpha. The user confirmed alignment on the definition of alpha.
